posts.title: 2026.33: The CapEx Train Keeps Rolling
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of August 10, 2026, including the capital constraint, AI writing, and a tale of two cities.
bullets: The AI industry is shifting from compute and power constraints to a potential capital constraint, as current AI investments have yet to demonstrate clear, self-sustaining profitability.

Nvidia is employing new financial engineering mechanisms to access long-duration capital, a move intended to bridge the revenue gap but which simultaneously increases the systemic risk to their profit margins.

Regulatory mandates, such as the EU's requirement to label AI-generated text, are being criticized for potentially stifling innovation and failing to account for the evolving societal acceptance of AI-assisted content.

The divergence between New York City's resilient financial hub and Hollywood's declining production base illustrates how network effects can protect some industries from political pressure while leaving others vulnerable to geographic outsourcing.

posts.title: Li Auto's chip ambitions extend from assisted driving to data centers, report says
posts.summary:
Li Auto is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, and the project is still at an early stage.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto is in the early stages of developing an in-house cloud inference chip to handle workloads currently managed by GPUs.
The project aims to leverage the dataflow architecture used in the company's vehicle-side assisted driving chips to achieve cost efficiencies.
By reusing compute designs and software tools from its vehicle NPU, Li Auto seeks to optimize R&D spending while addressing the complex requirements of cloud-based large language model inference.
Success for the initiative depends on the company's ability to manage high-bandwidth memory and cluster scheduling while maintaining a competitive cost structure compared to standard GPU deployments.

posts.title: Li Auto's L6 tops 400,000 cumulative deliveries as revamped model revives demand
posts.summary:
The Li L6 delivered about 9,000 units in the first half of August, compared with just 2,716 for the whole of July, based on CnEVPost-compiled data.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto's L6 SUV has surpassed 400,000 cumulative deliveries in less than 27 months, cementing its status as a core volume driver for the company.
Demand for the model has rebounded sharply following the July 16 launch of a revamped version, with approximately 9,000 units delivered in the first half of August alone.
The updated L6 features significant technical upgrades, including a 51 kWh battery for 300 km of all-electric range and the integration of the in-house Mach M100 assisted driving chip.
The successful refresh of the L6 is a critical component of Li Auto's broader strategy to modernize its L-series EREV lineup and recover from a mid-year sales slump.

posts.title: Geely Farizon's first overseas plant starts operations in Indonesia
posts.summary:
The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line on August 13 at a plant about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Farizon has commenced operations at its first overseas knock-down (KD) plant in Indonesia, located southeast of Jakarta.
The facility successfully rolled out its first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle on August 13, marking a shift toward localized production.
This strategy is designed to bypass import tariffs, streamline supply chains, and adapt vehicle specifications to local road conditions and tropical climates.
The company plans to gradually expand its localized product lineup and integrate further into the Indonesian industrial chain to support long-term growth in Southeast Asia.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Lam Research and ASE expansions; data center shifts; CPO system architecture initiative; 2D-transistor interface solution; USENIX HW security; patent suits; image sensors; programmable AI memtransistor; Nvidia's new plan; earnings; Tier IV's L4 auto chip.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: ASE subsidiary SPIL is investing $3.1 billion in a new Taiwan-based facility to expand CoWoS capacity for AI chips, with production slated for 2028.
Data center infrastructure is undergoing a major architectural shift toward 1-megawatt racks, necessitating significant changes in cooling, power delivery, and 3D-IC packaging.
Rhodium Group projects that China's legacy-chip capacity will reach nearly 50% of global output by 2030, even as the nation faces continued restrictions on leading-edge AI hardware.
Lam Research announced a $3 billion, five-year R&D expansion to increase its experimental capacity by 50%, alongside a workforce development partnership with NY Creates.
Industry experts are increasingly advocating for smaller, open-source AI models that reduce energy and water consumption by running on local hardware rather than massive data centers.
